extracted.intended_audience: public company registrants, securities lawyers, auditors, and compliance officers (and their advisers)
extracted.subtask_description: Interpretation and implementation guidance for registrants subject to the SEC's final climate-related disclosure and tagging rules, including compliance timelines, XBRL tagging, cost-estimation methods, and related definitional categories used in the economic analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Phase-in schedule for disclosure and tagging
rubrics_metrics.description: LAFs must begin complying with the disclosure requirements in filings covering fiscal year 2025 and must comply with the tagging requirements in filings covering fiscal year 2026. Other categories of filers must comply with the tagging requirements upon their initial compliance with the climate disclosure rules. For example, AFs must comply with tagging requirements when they first provide climate disclosures in filings covering fiscal year 2026.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Phase-in periods cause registrants to incur compliance costs at different times; for comparability the estimates are presented as the average annual compliance cost over the first ten years of compliance. See section II.N and cited CFR provisions for specific timing by filer category.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inline XBRL structuring of filing fee information (July 2024)
rubrics_metrics.description: Beginning in July 2024, filers of most fee-bearing forms will be required to structure filing fee information in Inline XBRL (see 17 CFR references).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commission will provide an optional web tool that will allow filers to provide those tagged disclosures without the use of Inline XBRL compliance services or software. See 17 CFR 229.601(b)(107); 17 CFR 232.408 and Filing Fee Disclosure and Payment Methods Modernization release.

rubrics_metrics.name: Benefits of XBRL/Inline XBRL tagging
rubrics_metrics.description: Empirical studies indicate XBRL reporting facilitates generation and infusion of idiosyncratic information into the market, improves market efficiency, levels the informational playing field between insiders and non-insiders, and can provide larger incremental informational value relative to HTML filings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Findings (not necessarily climate-specific) suggest XBRL-tagged disclosures improve relevance, understandability, comparability, analyst forecast properties, and reduce information processing costs. The final rules anticipate similar investor benefits from climate-related XBRL tagging.

rubrics_metrics.name: Informational benefits of custom/extended XBRL tags
rubrics_metrics.description: Studies have found informational benefits resulting from the proper use of custom tags (extended XBRL tags).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Research (e.g., Joseph Johnston) finds custom tags are robustly negatively related to analysts' forecast error and dispersion, supporting the benefit of appropriate use of custom tags when needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope 3 emissions disclosure not required by final rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The final rules do not require Scope 3 emissions reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenter concerns about burdens for non-registrants focused on Scope 3; the final rules were revised from the proposal in ways intended to reduce burden and explicitly exclude a requirement to report Scope 3 emissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: No mandatory requirement to use third-party services
rubrics_metrics.description: The final rules impose no requirement with respect to the use of third-party services; registrants are free to decide how best to meet compliance based on their specific circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registrants required to disclose emissions or facing complex climate-related risks may be more likely to engage third-party services, but use of such services is optional and not mandated by the rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Governance, strategy, and risk-management disclosure cost categories (definitions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Governance costs include the ongoing cost to those in scope to implement, document and disclose governance of their climate-related risks and opportunities and to coordinate across internal business functions. Strategy costs include the ongoing reporting costs to coordinate, document and disclose climate-related risks and opportunities identified and report the impact of these risks on business, strategy, and financial planning. Risk management costs are the ongoing annual costs to disclose the company's management of climate-related risks, including coordination across functions, identification and assessment of risks and integration into the company's overarching risk-management strategy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scenario analysis costs are discussed separately. These definitional categories are used to aggregate and compare cost estimates (e.g., in comparisons with FCA/BEIS analyses) and differences in cost assumptions (e.g., internal labor assumptions) can drive discrepancies across estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Survey category definitions for cost components
rubrics_metrics.description: Survey categories used in cost estimation include: (a) costs relating to the development of GHG inventories with analysis and disclosure of Scope 1, Scope 2, and/or Scope 3 emissions; (b) costs related to conducting assessments of climate risks using scenario analysis and related TCFD/CDP disclosures; (c) additional voluntary climate-related analyses and disclosures disconnected from the proposed rules (outreach, engagement, management); and (d) costs for internal climate risk management controls (integration into ERM, board oversight, strategic planning, internal audit, data collection and aggregation including IT costs and staff time, internal and external legal review).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these category definitions when mapping commenter survey responses to the cost-estimation framework; respondents were asked to exclude overlap between categories where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost-estimation methodology: averaging and use of medians
rubrics_metrics.description: Because registrants will incur compliance costs at different times due to phase-in periods, the estimates are presented as the average annual compliance cost over the first ten years of compliance. Throughout the cost estimation process, medians are used instead of means because medians are less sensitive to outliers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The release provides arithmetic examples (e.g., ($327,000 + $183,000*(9 years))/10 = $197,400) to illustrate the averaging approach and notes total compliance costs are calculated each year and then averaged across the first ten years.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paperwork Reduction Act (PRA) labor cost assumptions
rubrics_metrics.description: The PRA assumes that internal burden hours cost $444/hour, while external burden hours cost $600/hour.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These assumptions feed into the PRA burden-hour cost calculations; see section V for more detail and for use in economic analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of foreign regulatory cost estimates and currency-conversion assumptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Cost estimates from foreign rules (e.g., BEIS, FCA) are incorporated with currency conversion using the 2022 average exchange rate (e.g., $1.2369 USD/GBP for BEIS and $1.0538 USD/EUR for other referenced conversions), rounded as described.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: BEIS/FCA cost estimates were treated as if affected entities had no pre-existing climate-related disclosure practices; familiarization and legal-review cost components from BEIS were specifically cited and converted to USD using the stated rates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of commenter cost estimates that include voluntary activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Commenters' estimates that include the cost of voluntarily undertaking a specific activity (e.g., costs of setting targets or goals, formulating transition plans, or conducting scenario analysis) may not be indicative of the compliance costs of the final rules because the final rules do not necessarily require undertaking such activities but may require only attendant disclosures in certain cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When commenter submissions mixed voluntary activity costs with costs directly attributable to the rules (e.g., TCFD costs), the Commission used only the directly relevant portions (omitting unrelated sustainability-consultant costs when they could not be reliably apportioned) to avoid overestimating compliance costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-scaling cost components and disproportionate impacts on smaller registrants
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain components of compliance costs may not vary with firm size and may be higher in proportional terms for smaller registrants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The economic analysis recognizes that per-dollar impacts can be proportionally larger for smaller entities; cost estimates and burden analyses should account for fixed or non-scalable elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of financial-statement estimates impacted by severe weather or disclosed targets/transition plans
rubrics_metrics.description: The incremental costs considered include the disclosure of financial statement estimates and assumptions materially impacted by severe weather events and other conditions or disclosed targets or transition plans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The release notes these incremental costs are expected to be minimal, but they are explicitly included in the overall compliance-cost accounting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of CDP-to-TCFD cost ratio in cost conversions
rubrics_metrics.description: Based on commenter statements that it takes designated staff four months to complete the CDP questionnaire and nine months to complete TCFD disclosures, the analysis incorporates an assumption that the CDP-to-TCFD cost ratio is 4-to-9.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This ratio was used to map costs reported for CDP to equivalent TCFD-cost estimates where necessary and is sourced from letters from Soc. Corp. Gov.
